chapter: Building the band, Ivie Anderson and touring
title: Bubber Miley joins and the band turns from sweet to growl
summary: Greer says Bubber and Tricky turned the sweet band to growl; Bubber auditioned in 1925.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: : Arthur Whetsel, right, and then after Whetsel, Bubber Miley came in the band, right.
: They came in after. What about -- I read somewhere once that Duke Ellington said that until the band played what he called sweet music; until --
: And then when he heard Bubber Miley.

Then Bubber and Tricky would turn it around. We still played sweet music but we -- little by little it come to the growl and things, you know, because Tricky growled and Bubber growled and of course, we still played sweet too, but the majority of it was growling.
: Do you remember when you first heard Bubber Miley?

I'm trying to remember. When I first heard Bubber Miley. No, I never knew him until he came down to the Kentucky Club, that's the first time I heard him. I seen him, but not to play I never heard him. I knew him as a guy but I never heard him play.
In fact, I never heard him and Duke never heard him till he come down to play with us.
: He sat in with the band?
He came out -- we were trying to select a guy to replace Whetsel and he tried, he tried out for it.
Did you agree that that was the one which should come in?
Yeah, he was something else. Everybody liked him. He was new and he was different. Nobody played like him, and Duke had the ear for unique guys, so he got the job.
Now, at that time, during that period of -- this was about what, 1925, '25 and '26, around in there.
1925 when he came in the band and then shortly after him, Sidney Bechet came in the band?
